summary:
**Artemis Base Camp: Junior Outpost Commander** is a 100% offline-first, interactive deep-space survival simulator designed for youth aged 7–12, educators, and science communicators for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Challenge 03: *Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer*).

Built with zero external dependencies using pure HTML5, CSS3, and deterministic vanilla ES6 modules, the trainer places players in command of a four-person outpost at the Moon’s Shackleton Crater or Mars’s Jezero Crater. Players balance four interconnected survival gauges—Power Grid, Oxygen Purity, Water Reserves, and Radiation Shielding—learning the fundamental aerospace engineering principle that "there is no free lunch in space."

Every calculation is grounded in real NASA open datasets (DONKI, OSDR/GeneLab, LRO LOLA/Diviner, Mars 2020 MEDA, and MOXIE), transparently cited in an in-game Evidence & Provenance Drawer. This approach transforms abstract astrophysics and life-support math into engaging, hands-on decision-making, inspiring the next generation of explorers with scientifically accurate, resilient STEM education.
details:
Artemis Base Camp: Junior Outpost Commander is a 100% offline-first, interactive deep-space survival simulator created for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Challenge 03: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, Youth / Intermediate Category). Designed for learners aged 7–12, educators, and science communicators, the project teaches fundamental aerospace systems engineering—specifically the principle that "there is no free lunch in space"—across two real-world planetary destinations: Shackleton Crater at the Lunar South Pole and Jezero Crater on Mars.

What It Does & How It Works

Players assume command of a four-person deep-space outpost over a five-Sol mission cycle, balancing four interconnected survival subsystems in real time:

  • Power Grid (kW / Battery %): Balances diurnal solar array generation and a constant 10 kW Kilopower nuclear fission reactor against energy sinks including ECLSS scrubbers, water heaters, surface rovers, and electromagnetic shields.
  • Oxygen Air (% Purity): Models human metabolic consumption (0.84 kg O₂/person/day) maintained by Sabatier and MOXIE CO₂-to-O₂ electrolysis units that throttle down if power reserves drop.
  • Water Supply (Liters / % Recycled): Tracks crew hydration needs (2.5 L/person/day) supported by closed-loop greywater recycling (up to 85% recovery) and power-intensive ice core drilling.
  • Radiation & Force Shields (% Shielding / Cumulative mSv): Simulates continuous Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR) alongside acute Solar Particle Events (SPE) and Coronal Mass Ejections (CME). Players can activate electromagnetic force shields that block 90% of radiation to keep crew exposure below the 50 mSv NCRP Report 153 safety threshold—at the cost of a heavy +18 kW battery drain.

Every calculation runs inside a deterministic simulation engine (sim.js) backed by an in-game Evidence & Provenance Drawer that maps each parameter directly to official NASA open datasets (DONKI, OSDR/GeneLab, LRO LOLA, LRO Diviner, Mars 2020 MEDA, and Mars MOXIE). Surviving to Sol 05 unlocks a dynamically generated Junior Flight Director Certificate downloadable as a PNG.

Tools, Languages & Technical Architecture

  • Languages & Standards: Pure HTML5, CSS3, and modern vanilla ES6 JavaScript modules—built with zero build tools, zero frameworks, and zero runtime dependencies so the application launches instantaneously via file:// or any static web server.
  • Offline-First Data Layer: All planetary constants, thermal curves, and space-weather baselines are pre-cached in local JSON fixtures (data/nasa_reference.json and demo_fixtures/nasa_reference.json), guaranteeing uninterrupted operation in classrooms, science museums, and low-connectivity environments.
  • Graphics & Procedural Audio: A custom 960×520 HTML5 2D Canvas engine renders an interactive, living colony (rotating solar masts, pulsing Kilopower reactor, forcefield dome, ice drills, rovers, and EVA astronauts), paired with a native Web Audio API synthesizer that generates retro space sound effects and alarms procedurally without external .mp3 files.
  • Testing & Licensing: Verified with a deterministic unit test suite (tests/test_sim.js), comprehensive documentation (MANUAL.md, docs/AI_USE.md), and released under the open-source Apache-2.0 License.

Creativity, Design Considerations & Intended Impact

  • Accessibility & Classroom Readiness: Our team prioritized zero-friction deployment for teachers and students. On desktop monitors (≥900px), the UI locks into a zero-scroll mission control cockpit so every gauge and interactive element remains visible at once; on tablets and phones (≤768px), it adapts into a vertical touch layout with 44px+ hit targets and haptic feedback.
  • Scientific Authenticity Over Magic Buttons: Rather than abstracting resource management into simple arcade power-ups, we engineered causal feedback loops where turning on a life-saving shield forces immediate trade-offs in rover operations or ice mining.
  • Intended Impact: By turning real NASA telemetry and physics equations into tactile, visual cause-and-effect gameplay, Artemis Base Camp empowers young learners to think like flight directors—demystifying spaceflight engineering and inspiring the next generation of Artemis explorers.
